cues: A free hydrogen ion is just a bare proton, about ten to the minus fifteen metres across, with an enormous charge density.
In water, it is grabbed at once by a water molecule, forming the hydronium ion, H three O plus.
text: Two. A free hydrogen ion is just a bare proton, about ten to the minus fifteen metres across, with an enormous charge density. It cannot float around alone. In water, it is grabbed at once by a water molecule, forming the hydronium ion, H three O plus.
